title: Capacity preflight cheatsheet - personal prep
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick personal checklist for 1:1 with capacity PM and for weekly pool syncs. Not a formal doc — scratchpad to keep the conversation focused.
- Focus areas: short-term reservation asks, burst/autoscale polish, and a 6–12 week forecast sanity check for Dedicated GPU pools.

Agenda bullets (30m):
- 5m: quick state (what changed since last week: 2 new product rollouts, one big eval job landed)
- 10m: reservation ask & rationales (who needs what, risk if denied)
- 8m: autoscale thresholds + burst budget (tuning proposal)
- 5m: action items and immediate blockers (tickets/infra work)

Quick facts to have on hand (numbers to cite):
- Current committed pool: 24x A100-80GB equivalents (mix of 8x H100, 16x A100 in terms of perf).
- Avg sustained nightly throughput (tokens/minute across hosted v. dedicated): ~1.2M tokens/minute for two peak windows (US morning + APAC evening).
- Peak concurrent model slots in Dedicated this month: 14 (but projected cross-team spike to 22 if X feature + eval run overlap).
- Recent large job: partner-eval #2026-02 — consumed an unexpected 6 GPU-hours in burst window (no reservation).

Reservation ask draft (what I'll propose):
- Request +8 GPU-equivalent reservation for Q2 ramp (target start 2026-04-01), with 2-GPU burst headroom.
- Rationale: Predictable latency for customer-facing inference routes + avoid expensive on-demand during scheduled evals.
- Preference: reserve mixture (4 H100-equivalent, 4 A100-equivalent) to support both high-throughput and memory-heavy models.
- Fallback: if full +8 not approved, ask for +4 with auto-burst cap to 8.

Autoscale tuning notes (proposed thresholds):
- Scale-up policy: trigger additional nodes when route-level p95 latency > 500ms for >= 2 minutes AND queue depth > 30.
- Scale-down policy: wait 10 minutes of healthy p50/p95 before scale down to avoid thrash.
- Burst budget: 200 GPU-hours per week pooled across teams (assignable). Track burn rate daily.
- Tip: propose a canary throttle — only allow burst for non-prod/staging first for 48 hours.

Cost / risk shorthand (to mention):
- Immediate cost delta: rough estimate +8 reservation = +$32k/mo (ballpark, check finance calc).
- Risk of not reserving: increased tail latency + higher per-token cost for peak on-demand runs, potential SLO breaches for 3 paid customers.
- Operational risk: more manual orchestration if we maintain small pools per team. Advocate for shared pool with strong tagging/cost chargeback.

Forecast heuristics (6–12 week window):
- Best case: product growth absorbed by smarter batching/caching -> no extra reservation needed; push for Optimize config changes first.
- Mid case: +4 reservation (autoscale to +8) to handle overlapping rollouts in 6 weeks.
- Worst case: +12 reservation (unlikely) if two enterprise customers concurrently ramp and eval jobs double.

Questions I want answered in the meeting (write down the ask):
- Can we get detailed token-level billing for the last 30 days broken down by route (hosting vs dedicated)? (Who: Finance/Observability)
- Is there a hard limit on burst capacity per org? If yes, what is the policy and how is it enforced? (Who: infra)
- Are there planned infra maintenance windows in April that would conflict with the proposed reservation start?

Follow-ups / action items (note to self — assign after meeting):
- [Sofia] Build a simple 6-week simulation in sheet form (inputs: current pool, queued jobs distribution, projected ramp %) — due 2026-03-18.
- [Maya] Pull token-level / route-level usage for Feb 15–Mar 10 and tag suspected eval jobs — due 2026-03-12.
- [Julian] PoC for burst throttle (48h canary) on a non-prod pool; report perf metrics — due 2026-03-22.
- [Arjun] Confirm cost delta with finance and return a low/medium/high estimate — due 2026-03-15.
- [Infra] Note: if reservation approved, coordinate network/KMS preflight for Private deploy tests (ticket INF-4821).

Notes to self / talking points (short):
- Emphasize predictability > micro-savings — product leads will trade cost for SLA.
- Keep autoscale conservative; avoid oscillation (we burned cycles fixing thrash last quarter).
- Push for tagging discipline now (cost attribution will justify reservation asks).

Loose scratch calculations (quick):
- If 1 H100 ~ 1.8x A100 perf for our workloads, then +8 equiv = could be 3 H100 or mix 2 H100 + 4 A100; sanity check with SLOs.
- Peak concurrency projection: current 14 -> predicted 22 = +8 slots; if avg job length 45m, that's ~6 extra GPU-hours per hour during peak windows -> validate with Maya's usage dump.

Local bookmarks / refs (to copy into formal ask later):
- Confluence: dedicated-gpu-runbook (for reservation process)
- Slack thread: #capacity-planning-thread (Feb 24 discussion re: burst budgets)
- JIRA: INF-4821 (preflight checklist for private infra)

Rough script for the 1:1 opener: 
"Prep: quick snapshot. Goal: land +4 reserved now, negotiate +4 as soft-burst. If we can get finance and infra aligned this week, I'll schedule the configuration cutover for April 1. Also want agreement to run a 48h burst canary on non-prod before enabling for prod routes."

Open questions I still have (to record):
- How will chargeback appear on product invoices? Need template.
- Can we auto-assign burst credits per team in Console today, or is that an infra change?

End-of-note: keep this as personal scratchpad — will turn into a short proposal doc if we get buy-in.
